headline: Saudi Says It Destroyed Missiles Bound for Riyadh
deck: The coalition also reported drone interceptions in the Eastern Province, with no stated casualties or damage from the missile attack.
body: Saudi-led coalition air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh, the coalition said. Turki al-Maliki, the coalition spokesperson, said Yemen’s Houthi group launched the missiles; he gave no details of casualties or damage. The National said the kingdom was facing attacks against the capital, oil infrastructure and Red Sea ports [E1][E2][E4].

The coalition also reported intercepting and destroying two drones over the Eastern Province, The National said [E5]. Explosions echoed above Riyadh, Gulf News reported, a day after the Houthis claimed strikes on the capital [E8]. Saudi forces said they also destroyed a cruise missile in the country’s west and a drone near Jeddah port [E9].

The Houthis said they had attacked the ports of Jeddah and Jazan in retaliation for coalition strikes on Hodeidah port, and did not identify the weapons used, aa.com.tr reported [E3]. The National said there was no immediate confirmation that Jeddah port had been hit [E6]. Yahya Saree, the Houthi military spokesperson, had threatened retaliation against Saudi Red Sea ports if the coalition struck Hodeida [E10]. Since the coalition’s Wednesday report that four drones were destroyed over Ras Tanura without saying the facility was hit, the current account adds the reported Riyadh missile interceptions and the two Eastern Province drones [E7].
